author: haiku
label: climb-04-01
changes: Terms section: added attempt, queue retry, lease, heartbeat, checkpoint, multipart upload and stale, so each step can be read on its own (Q6).
Step 1: listed the three response shapes (200 CSV, 202 JSON, error JSON) and how the page tells them apart (Q1).
Step 4.1: a done row with empty emailed_at now goes to Step 7, not a plain return (Q2).
Step 4.2: a live lease now makes the attempt raise instead of return normally, and the lease condition covers the stale case (Q4, Q5).
Removed the completing state from the table, Step 6 and the page. A failed completion is handled by an object-exists check (Q3).
Heartbeat is now written after each replica page as well as each part. Stale means older than 5 minutes, set on the server, replacing the 35-minute rule (Q5, Q7).
A raised attempt now sets the row to queued with an error text before re-raising, so the page can show a pending retry (Q7).
Step 8.2: the final-failure update no longer checks lease_token (Q8).

Step 9.3: the page and download now end at expires_at (24 hours), matching the email link, instead of 7 days. The bucket's 7-day lifecycle still removes files. This follows the brief's 24-hour link rule (decided).
Moved the build steps and constants into a separate 'Before building' section, away from the runtime flow. Merged the old Step 0 items into B1 to B4.
Added a failure table at the end, so the failure paths can be checked together.
Removed repeated justifications and merged duplicated size and timing notes into Step 5.
Open questions: added 10 (duplicate job delivery), 11 (no object-exists helper in storage.py, and whether a repeated part number replaces the part) and 12 (the 5-minute STALE_AFTER is a guess).
Moved the summary and terms to the top, and cut the separate Overview and repeated flow description, so the document opens with what the system is and how the main flow goes.
Removed the codes that sent the reader elsewhere (B1 to B4, open question numbers, Q-style references). Sub-steps are now lettered within each step, and each step stands alone.
Gave every step the same parts (Starts, Does, Keeps, When it fails). Folded the Step 8 'unless the row is done' rule into its first sub-step, with the same behaviour.
Moved the one-time build work (shared query and CSV writer, table, email templates, constants) into its own section, kept apart from how the system runs.
Moved the storage check (object exists, and part re-upload replaces the earlier part) from open questions into a build step, since it is work to do rather than a decision.
Merged open questions 1 and 12 (replica speed and STALE_AFTER) into one timing question, because both depend on the same measurements.
Merged open questions 5 and 6 (unfiltered and stale row_count) into one row-count question.
Merged open question 7 (email templates) into a single line on the email system; kept it as an open question because it is unconfirmed.
Turned open question 8 (export history) into a stated decision in Step 3's Keeps section, since it is settled, not open.
Shortened the page-response explanation in Step 1 and the rebuild and duplicate-delivery notes. No behaviour was changed; every failure path and state transition from the original is kept.
